notable_results: Davide Ongaro won the 2024 IFMAR 1:8 IC Off-Road World Championship driving the RC8B4.1; latest of Associated's championship buggy line. An RC8B4.1e electric variant also exists.
notes: Current reigning World Champion platform (2024).

notable_results: Davide Ongaro won the 2022 IFMAR 1:8 IC Off-Road World Championship driving the RC8B4, becoming the first two-time IFMAR 1:8 World Champion.
notes: 2022 Worlds-winning platform; has an RC8B4e e-buggy sibling.

notable_results: Evolution of the RC8B3.1 platform that won the 2018 IFMAR Worlds (Ongaro) and 2019 ROAR Nationals (Rivkin); widely raced in A-mains in the late 2010s.
notes: Late-2010s competition staple; RC8B3.2e electric variant exists.

notable_results: Davide Ongaro won the 2018 IFMAR 1:8 IC Off-Road World Championship in Perth on the RC8B3.1; Spencer Rivkin won the ROAR 1:8 Fuel Off-Road Nationals with it.
notes: 2018 Worlds winner; foundation of the RC8B3.x family.

notable_results: Newest Inferno (2025) and first full model change since the MP10; continuation of the Inferno line that holds eight IFMAR 1:8 buggy Worlds titles.
notes: Latest competition Inferno; just entering race rotation.

notable_results: Launched Jan 2019; the TKI3 version incorporated components developed for the 2022 IFMAR Worlds. Long-running A-main Inferno platform with a TQ-pedigree heritage.
notes: MP10e electric e-buggy variant exists; TKI2/TKI3 spec updates.

notable_results: TQ in qualifying and 2nd place finish at the 2016 IFMAR 1:8 Off-Road Worlds in Las Vegas; one of the most successful and long-raced Infernos.
notes: Older but still-raced classic; MP9e TKI4 electric variant exists.

notable_results: Cody King won the 2010 IFMAR 1:8 IC Off-Road World Championship driving the Kyosho Inferno MP9 TKI2.
notes: 2010 Worlds winner; historically significant older platform.

notable_results: Ryan Maifield won The Dirt Nitro Challenge, Silver State Nitro Challenge, and ROAR 1:8 Fuel Nationals in 2021 with the MBX8R geometry.
notes: MBX8R ECO electric e-buggy variant exists.

notable_results: Mugen ran four MBX8s in the 60-minute final at the 2018 IFMAR Worlds with Ryan Maifield finishing on the podium; the Worlds Edition packages the team's 2018 Worlds option parts.
notes: Worlds Edition trim; MBX8 ECO electric variant exists.

notable_results: Robert Batlle won the 2012 IFMAR 1:8 IC Off-Road World Championship driving the Mugen MBX-7.
notes: 2012 Worlds winner; older but a landmark Mugen platform.

notable_results: Top-tier TLR competition nitro buggy building on the championship-winning 8IGHT heritage; raced at major US and international 1:8 events.
notes: 8IGHT-XE Elite electric and 8IGHT-X/E 2.0 nitro/electric combo variants exist.

notable_results: TLR's mainline 1:8 nitro buggy of the late 2010s with updated suspension geometry and drivetrain; a regular A-main contender.
notes: Predecessor to the 8IGHT-X Elite.

notable_results: Production version of the prototype HB team drivers ran at the 2022 IFMAR Worlds in Spain; delivers quicker lap times than the D819RS.
notes: Current HB flagship nitro buggy (2022 Worlds prototype).

notable_results: Race-spec evolution of the World Champion D819 line; widely raced in A-mains in the late 2010s/early 2020s.
notes: RS = Race Spec update of the D819.

notable_results: Successor in HB's World Champion buggy line (following the Worlds-winning D815/D817), adding latest high-performance parts.
notes: Branded 'World Champion' line continuation.

notable_results: David Ronnefalk won the 2016 IFMAR Worlds in Las Vegas; back-to-back World titles for the D815 and D817.
notes: 2016 Worlds winner (HB-branded successor to the Hot Bodies D815).

notable_results: Ty Tessmann won the 2014 IFMAR 1:8 IC Off-Road World Championship driving the Hot Bodies D812.
notes: 2014 Worlds winner under the Hot Bodies brand (predecessor to HB Racing).

notable_results: ROAR National Championship-winning buggy in the hands of Ryan Maifield; podium in seven of the past ten major US 1:8 events.
notes: Seventh revision of the NB48 series; EB48 2.x is the electric sibling platform.

notable_results: Widely raced chassis that the NB48 2.2 builds on; strong rough-track A-main performer in US national events.
notes: Direct predecessor to the NB48 2.2.

notable_results: Original NB48 competition nitro buggy that established Tekno as a 1:8 off-road race contender in the US.
notes: Foundation of the long-running NB48 series.

notable_results: Latest evolution of the XB8 line that has won EFRA Euros (Bruno Coelho), ROAR Nationals (Ty Tessmann) and taken Worlds Vice-Champion.
notes: XB8E is the electric sibling; annual model-year refreshes.

notable_results: Part of the XB8 platform that won the EFRA European Championship (Bruno Coelho), a ROAR National title (Ty Tessmann) and was Worlds Vice-Champion (Tessmann, 2018).
notes: Model-year 2024 spec of the XB8.

notable_results: XB8'19 spec from the platform that delivered XRAY's EFRA Euro title and ROAR National title and Worlds Vice-Champion (Ty Tessmann TQ, 2018).
notes: Late-2010s XB8 spec; representative of the heavily raced era.

notable_results: Factory-developed competition nitro buggy with hard-anodized lightened chassis and short-wheelbase design; SWORKz's current top 1:8 race platform tested by factory pilots.
notes: S35-4E EVO is the brushless/e-buggy sibling.

notable_results: SWORKz's mainline Pro nitro competition buggy widely sold and raced internationally; base of the S35-4 EVO development.
notes: S35-4 platform; electric variants exist.

notable_results: Newcomer competition buggy; a development version ran at the FEMCA Championships in Taiwan, qualifying 3rd for the main and finishing 5th in the 50-minute final.
notes: F8e is the electric variant; shaft-drive 4WD, ~323-327mm wheelbase.

notable_results: Agama's competition 1:8 nitro buggy used by the team with good results; iterated through A319P Performance and 2022-spec versions.
notes: A319P and 2022-spec trims; successor to the earlier Agama A8. A319E is the electric sibling.

notable_results: Serpent's competition 1:8 nitro off-road buggy, based on the SRX8 Evo, with redesigned diffs and steering for long-main durability.
notes: SRX8e PRO is the electric/brushless variant of the Cobra SRX8 platform.

notable_results: Team Associated's first competition 1/8 e-buggy, derived from the RC8B3 nitro platform; widely raced in ROAR 1:8 e-buggy nationals and EOS electric off-road.
notes: ASC80916. Electric version of the RC8B3 nitro buggy.

notable_results: Updated B3.1e built from RC8B3.1 nitro engineering; a regular A-main car at ROAR electric off-road nationals.
notes: ASC80936. Successor to RC8B3e.

notable_results: 4x4 electric buggy from the RC8B4 generation; campaigned in ROAR 1:8 e-buggy nationals and EOS electric off-road.
notes: ASC80946. Team kit.

notable_results: Won the inaugural 2024 IFMAR 1:8 Electric Off-Road World Championship in Barcelos, Portugal (Marcus Kaerup). Offers front/rear weight-bias chassis options.
notes: ASC80950. Inaugural 1:8 E-Buggy World Champion chassis.

notable_results: Tekno's redesigned-geometry 1/8 e-buggy of its era; a long-running A-main competitor in ROAR electric off-road nationals and EOS (Bornhorst/Tebo).
notes: TKR5005. A SuperLight EB48.3SL (TKR5004) variant also existed.

notable_results: Easier-to-drive evolution with increased rear traction; campaigned at ROAR 1:8 electric nationals and EOS by Tekno factory drivers Joe Bornhorst and Jared Tebo.
Major redesign (revised shock towers, Ackerman spindle plates, tall wing mount, stronger gearboxes); raced by Tekno team at ROAR electric off-road nationals and EOS.
New rear arms/hubs with adjustable roll center and very long (112mm) arms; campaigned in ROAR 1:8 electric nationals and EOS by Tekno factory team.
Won the ROAR 2023 1:8 Electric Off-Road Nationals; eighth iteration of the EB48 series, run by Joe Bornhorst and Jared Tebo to frequent podiums.
notes: TKR9005. Current-generation EB48 electric.

notable_results: TLR's first ground-up dedicated 1/8 4WD electric race buggy on the championship-winning 8IGHT lineage; raced by TLR drivers (Dakotah Phend, Barry Baker, Brian Kinney) with published kit/event setup sheets.
notes: TLR04008. Manuals and driver setup sheets are linked from the TLR/Horizon product page.

notable_results: Top-spec Elite variant (Sept 2020) of the 8IGHT-XE with updated suspension geometry and drivetrain; used by TLR's factory race team at ROAR 1:8 electric nationals and EOS.
notes: TLR04011. Elite trim sharing the 8IGHT-XE platform.

notable_results: Combo kit buildable as nitro (8IGHT-X) or electric (8IGHT-E); the electric build is raced in ROAR 1:8 e-buggy nationals and EOS.
notes: TLR04012. Convertible nitro/electric kit; qualifies on its electric (8IGHT-E) configuration.

notable_results: Prototype took the 2016 EFRA 1/8 E-Buggy Euros title with David Ronnefalk. Based on the World Champion D815 V2 nitro platform.
notes: HBS204035. First HB 1/8 e-buggy; start of the E817/E819/E8 lineage.

notable_results: 2019 Dirt Nitro Challenge (DNC) E-Buggy champion; the platform whose improvements were carried into the E819.
notes: Revised E817; parts backward-compatible with E817 and forward-compatible with E819.

notable_results: Evolution of the 2019 DNC E-Buggy champion E817 V2; longer wheelbase, new diffs. Widely raced at EOS/national level.
notes: +2mm wheelbase vs E817 V2; thicker center brace, 43/13 diffs.

notable_results: Latest-spec E819 with team development features (V3 rear shock tower, adjustable wing/body-mount height); raced internationally at EOS and IFMAR-level events.
notes: HBS204645. Sold without bodyshell. Official downloads at hbracing.com/downloads-en.

notable_results: 2023 flagship e-buggy derived from the D8 World Spec nitro platform; revised symmetrical suspension geometry for high-grip, high-speed tracks. Current HB EOS/Worlds-class entry.
notes: HBS204855. Successor to the E819 line; sold without bodyshell.

notable_results: Electric version of the championship-winning MBX8 nitro platform; HTD high-traction diffs standard. Platform used by Ryan Maifield for the 2021 ROAR 1/8 Electric Nationals win. Widely campaigned in ROAR/EOS e-buggy classes.
notes: Kit code E2022 (Team Edition MUGE2026). Original MBX8 ECO; base for later MBX8R ECO.

notable_results: Mugen's flagship 1/8 e-buggy on the MBX8R geometry; ran at the inaugural 2025 IFMAR 1:8 Electric Off-Road Worlds in Barcelos with Burak Kilic among top free-practice qualifiers. New pivot blocks, HTD diffs, IFMAR-legal wing.
notes: Kit code E2028 (US MUGE2028). Successor to MBX8 ECO.

notable_results: 2018-spec electric flagship on the multiple-time World Champion XB8 platform; race-proven by the XRAY factory team. Start of the modern annual XB8E line.
notes: XRAY releases the XB8E as annual editions. Setup-sheet database on teamxray.com.

notable_results: Won the European Championships with Jean-Pierrick Sartel; developed/endorsed by World Champion Ty Tessmann and EC-winning factory drivers (Bayer, Matias, Savoya).
notes: Annual edition. European Championship-winning spec.

notable_results: 2024 competition edition of the XB8E annual line; the XB8 platform's first ROAR National Champion title (Ty Tessmann) plus continued EOS/European campaigning by the XRAY factory team.
notes: Annual edition, kit XRA350161.

notable_results: 2025 competition edition of the XB8E annual line; current-generation XRAY 1/8 e-buggy raced at EOS/IFMAR-level events.
notes: Annual edition, kit XRA350162.

notable_results: Electric version of the MP9 TKI4 competition platform (longer front arms, updated front shock stay, rear wing); inherits the nitro TKI4's pedigree (TQ + 2nd at the 2016 IFMAR 1/8 GP Off-Road Worlds, Las Vegas).
Brushless 4WD competition buggy with revised chassis layout and body for improved weight distribution; part of the Inferno race family. A later V2 Readyset (#34111) extends the same platform.
notes: Kit #34105B (released July 2018); V2 Readyset is #34111.

notable_results: Electric evolution of the MP10 competition platform (4S brushless, spread-battery layout) for the international 1/8 e-buggy class; built on the Inferno race lineage that holds multiple IFMAR 1/8 GP off-road world titles.
notes: Released June 2020 (kit #34110).

notable_results: Competition-revised MP10e: smaller/lighter diffs to cut rotational mass plus shock springs developed for the 2022 1/8 GP Buggy World Championship and updated aero body. Carries the Inferno GP-racing pedigree into the electric class.

Electric counterpart of the S35-3 nitro buggy, developed from the success of the S35-2E; adopted the latest nitro buggy's rear suspension, front Ackermann and new center diff. Raced in 1/8 e-buggy competition.
notes: Third-generation electric buggy. Official editable setup-sheet PDF verified live.

notable_results: Won the 2022 EFRA European Championship (1/8 E-Buggy) with Juan Carlos Canas in Slovakia, commemorated by an official 'European Champion Edition' kit. Follow-up S35-4e EVO uses BBS pistons/shock parts developed during the 2022 Worlds.
notes: Most competitive SWORKz 1/8 e-buggy (2022 EFRA Euros winner). Sold as S35-4E and later S35-4e EVO.

notable_results: Flagship 1/8 electric buggy at launch, with rear suspension and front Ackermann geometry from the S350 EVO II Limited nitro buggy and a new center transmission. Competed in club/national e-buggy racing.
notes: Second-generation electric buggy; bridges the S350 BE1 and S35-3E.

notable_results: SWORKz's first 1/8 E-Buggy race kit; as a prototype it reached the A-Main at the Nitro Challenge and AMS 3.0 and won 3 races. Later released as the S350 BE1 EVO and a USA Edition.
notes: First-generation SWORKz 1/8 electric buggy. Foundation of the S35-xE lineage.

notable_results: Electric version of the 2016 Cobra SRX8 nitro platform (designed by Billy Easton). Raced internationally on debut in 2017 — Easton at the Dirt Nitro Challenge, Joern Neumann and Shin Adachi at the Xiamen race in China.
notes: SER600018 (Pro). Shares suspension, shocks and gear-diffs with the Cobra SRX8 nitro.

notable_results: Serpent's first 1/8 competition e-buggy (~2013), derived from the 811 Cobra nitro platform; offered as kit (SER600004) and Be-RTR. Campaigned by Serpent team drivers in European electric off-road events.
notes: Original electric Cobra; electric sibling of the 811 Cobra nitro. Evolved into the Cobra E 2.1.

notable_results: Dedicated (ground-up) 1/8 electric buggy announced Jan 2016, built around the proven A215 suspension geometry but designed for electric weight distribution and torque; per Agama 'tested and proven at big races throughout 2015.'
notes: Purpose-built electric (not a conversion). Sibling of the A215 nitro line.

notable_results: Electric variant of the successful A319 nitro buggy (2020), using A319 suspension and most drivetrain components with a purpose-designed clamping motor mount; a higher-spec A319EP followed in 2021. EOS multi-champion Michal Orlowski ran the A319/A319EP under Nemo Racing.
notes: Electric sibling of the A319 nitro; A319EP is the performance/pro version.

notable_results: Electric version of the N1 nitro buggy (announced 2023). Lay-down-shock, ultra-low-CG competition design with RAD (Rapid Access Diff) gearbox and DBS (Double Bearing System). Current Agama/Nemo Racing e-buggy.
notes: Newest Agama e-buggy; electric sibling of the N1 nitro.

notable_results: JQ Products' first 1/8 electric buggy; per the official LiveRC release it took multiple podiums and wins at US Grassroots and JBRL events, a win at the Russian RedBull GP, and a win at the Rhein Main Warm Up in Germany.
notes: JQ's electric 1/8 buggy is named 'THE eCar'; shares gearboxes with the nitro THE Car.

notable_results: Truggy counterpart of the championship-winning RC8B3 buggy platform; campaigned by the Team Associated factory team (Spencer Rivkin, Ryan Cavalieri) at major US events including the Dirt Nitro Challenge and ROAR 1/8 Fuel Off-Road Nationals. RC8T3e is the brushless e-truggy sibling.
notes: Front-engine 1/8 nitro truggy, truggy version of the RC8B3. RC8T3e brushless sibling shares ~90% of parts.

notable_results: Mid-generation refresh (Feb 2018) with refined suspension framework for easier driving, more consistent lap times and increased durability; run by the AE off-road squad at ROAR and US national-level events. RC8T3.1e is the electric sibling.
notes: Updated RC8T3 (.1 revision), kit ASC80937. Electric RC8T3.1e (ASC80938).

notable_results: Released Sept 2020 (ASC80943), applying lessons from the RC8B3.2 buggy: flex-adjustable lengthened narrow-pivot rear arms, 4-piece center bulkhead, IFMAR-approved rear wing. Raced by the AE factory team at US ROAR-level nitro off-road events. RC8T3.2e electric variant released alongside.
notes: Final RC8T3-series revision before RC8T4, kit ASC80943. Electric RC8T3.2e (ASC80944).

notable_results: Current-generation AE 1/8 nitro truggy (kit ASC80947) with reduced-kingpin-inclination front geometry for stability and a 3.5-deg inclined front pinion. Campaigned by the AE factory off-road team at ROAR Fuel Off-Road Nationals. Electric RC8T4e took the 2024 ROAR Electric Truck National Title (Spencer Rivkin).
notes: Latest RC8T-series nitro truggy; shares manual with electric RC8T4e (Team Kit ASC80952).

notable_results: Released Sept 2015 with a front-engine-only chassis, trailing steering spindles and CNC brake discs. Ryan Lutz took 2nd in Truggy at the 2015 ROAR 1/8th Fuel Off-Road Nationals on the NT48.3. ET48.3 is the electric truggy sibling.
notes: Second-generation NT48 (.3 revision), kit TKR5406; front-engine layout. Electric sibling ET48.3.

notable_results: Released Nov 2021 (TKR9400); marketed as Tekno's fastest and most durable nitro truggy with quick-access diffs, very free suspension, twisted-caster front arms and a decoupled radio tray. ET48 2.0 (TKR9600) is the electric truggy sibling.
notes: Third-generation NT48, kit TKR9400. Electric sibling ET48 2.0.

notable_results: Released Feb 2025 (TKR9401) after 2+ years of US/Europe testing; secured back-to-back ROAR National Championships (Ryan Maifield) prior to public release. Latest NT48 generation. ET48 2.2 (TKR9605, Nov 2024) is the electric truggy sibling.
notes: Fourth-generation NT48 (Tekno skipped a 2.1 nitro truggy), kit TKR9401. Electric sibling ET48 2.2.

notable_results: 2014 ROAR Gas Off-Road Nationals (Thornhill Racing Circuit, TX): Dakotah Phend TQ'd and won the US National Truggy Championship on his 8IGHT-T 3.0, beating defending champ Ty Tessmann by ~0.3s; TLR was the best-represented brand with five 8IGHT-T 3.0s on the truggy grid.
notes: Kit TLR04001. Championship-winning generation; shares engineering with the ROAR-champion 8IGHT 3.0 buggy.

notable_results: Tanner Denney won Pro Nitro Truggy at the 2017 Psycho Nitro Blast on an 8IGHT-T 4.0. Platform contested ROAR Nationals and the Psycho Nitro Blast through the late 2010s with TLR drivers (Maifield, Phend, Denney) on team setup sheets.
notes: Kit TLR04005. 4mm 7075-T6 chassis, 16mm bore shocks, .21-.28 engine, 150cc tank.

notable_results: Current TLR race truggy; a single kit builds either nitro (8IGHT-XT) or electric (8IGHT-XTE). Dakotah Phend won the 2022 ROAR 1/8 Off-Road Nationals Nitro Truggy title; Ryan Maifield won the 2023 ROAR Nitro Off-Road Nationals Truggy class; Phend/Fuller traded Pro Truggy wins at the 2023 and 2026 Psycho Nitro Blast on the platform.
notes: Kit TLR04009; one kit = nitro XT or electric XTE.

notable_results: Kyosho's flagship competition truggy of the mid-2010s (released May 2015, kit 33004), built on the 8-time IFMAR World Championship Inferno chassis and sharing MP9 buggy drivetrain. Raced at EFRA Euros and ROAR-level 1/8 truggy class before the MP10T full model change.
notes: Kit 33004. New front/rear shock stays for high-grip; requires .21-.28 engine. Replaced by MP10T.

notable_results: Current-generation Kyosho competition truggy (kit 33017), a full model change from the ST-RR Evo.2, built on the IFMAR-winning MP10 buggy platform. Campaigned in modern 1/8 nitro truggy class events. MP10Te (kit 34115) is the brushless e-truggy variant.
notes: Kit 33017; .21-.28 engines. Electric sibling MP10Te (34115).

notable_results: Revised 'R' competition spec (MUGE2019) of the MBX-7T, part of Mugen's MBX-7 World Championship-era off-road lineup; campaigned in EFRA/ROAR-level 1/8 nitro truggy events. MBX7TR Eco (MUGE2020) is the electric variant.
notes: Kit MUGE2019; pivot-ball front suspension, 3mm hard-anodised chassis. Built on the Worlds-winning MBX-7 platform.

notable_results: 2021 ROAR Nitro Truggy National Champion. Built on the World-Championship MBX8 buggy platform with High Traction Differentials and a 3mm aluminium chassis; a dominant 1/8 nitro truggy of its era. MBX8T Eco (E2024) is the electric variant.
notes: Kit MUGE2023 (E2023) nitro; MBX8T Eco (E2024) electric. Shared E2023/E2024 manual covers both.

notable_results: Latest-generation Mugen competition truggy (MUGE2029); geometry developed through 2022 race conditions leading to many major victories, building on the 2021-ROAR-champion MBX8T lineage. New 4-shoe clutch and High Traction Differentials. MBX8TR ECO (MUGE2030) is the electric variant.
notes: Kit MUGE2029 (E2029) nitro; MBX8TR ECO (E2030) electric. Refined geometry over MBX8T.

notable_results: Replica of Ty Tessmann's championship truggy: 2012/2013 ROAR Nitro Truggy National Champion, 2012 and 2014 Dirt Nitro Challenge Pro Truggy Champion, 2014 ROAR Nationals Vice Champion, 2014 Pro-Line Dual Champion.
notes: HB Racing (formerly Hot Bodies/HPI) 1/8 nitro competition truggy on the Worlds-winning D8 platform. Precursor to D817T.

notable_results: Carries race DNA from the IFMAR World Champion D817 buggy; D817/E817-spec gearboxes, sintered brakes, 7075 symmetrical chassis. HB Racing's pro-class 1/8 nitro truggy of the late 2010s, campaigned at ROAR/EFRA-level events before the D8T Evo3. E817T is the electric sibling.
notes: Kit HB204170 (Pro combo HBS204332). Electric counterpart E817T.

notable_results: HB Racing's current World-Champion-branded competition truggy; updates the D817T to D819RS-style drivetrain, suspension mounts and sway bars with a new lightweight aluminum chassis. Marketed and campaigned as a race-winning pro-class 1/8 nitro truggy. E8T Evo3 is the electric sibling.
notes: Kit HBS204575; the D819-era truggy. Electric sibling E8T Evo3 (HB204576).

notable_results: World Champion Ty Tessmann brought the ROAR National Champion title to the XT8 platform. The XT8.2 (kit XRA350204) is a mid-cycle '.2' revision with all-new front suspension geometry; many wins across classes. XT8E.2 (XRA350300) is the electric variant.
notes: Kit XRA350204. Electric sibling XT8E.2.

notable_results: Latest XT8 generation (XT8'24/'25, kit XRA350206), designed with Martin Bayer, Ty Tessmann and Juraj Hudy; Tessmann carried the ROAR National Champion title on the XT8 platform. 4mm 7075-T6 chassis, 16mm big-bore shocks, quick-change diffs. XT8E'24 (350302) is the electric variant.
notes: Kit XRA350206 (sold as XT8'24/25). Semi-split V2 bulkheads. Electric sibling XT8E'24.

notable_results: Pure-racing successor to the S35-T (Jan 2021); SWORKz factory-team developed, widely raced in the 1/8 nitro truggy class. T7075 wide-layout chassis, new Truggy HET differentials, Speed Rhinoceros III body. S35-T2e (SW910040) is the brushless variant.
notes: Product code SW910039. Electric sibling S35-T2e (SW910040). A 2024 S35-T2 EVO (SW910043) further refines this platform.

notable_results: Durability-focused update of the Serpent Cobra Truggy on the Cobra 811 buggy platform; new diff couplers with larger bearings and larger upright bearings. Designer Billy Easton took 3rd at the 2011 CRCRC race with a production-prototype Cobra Truggy. Cobra 811TE (SER600033) is the electric variant.
notes: Kit SER600035. 3mm aluminum chassis, carbon shock towers, 16mm big-bore shocks, 150cc tank. Electric sibling Cobra 811TE (SER600033).

notable_results: Jon Hazlewood won the Pro-Line International Race on the A8T's race debut; developed over 12 months as Agama's competition 1/8 truggy on the A8 buggy platform. An electric A8T E-Truggy variant also exists.
notes: 17mm big bore shocks, centralized engine. A later A215T (on the A215 platform) is Agama's newer 1/8 nitro truggy.
